name: After Hours
oneLine: The family works at night: a near-black desk lit by one warm lamp overhead, charcoal windows set in bone-warm type, and the crab's terracotta as the only colour in the room.
rationale: It reads premium because it commits to one physical fiction and never breaks it: a single light source above the desktop, so every highlight is a 1px warm hairline on the TOP edge only, every shadow falls down, and the desk carries one amber glow at 50% -14% that the windows catch as a faint warm bounce in their outermost shadow. That single-source discipline is what separates a Braun or Teenage Engineering object from a skin — the 1995 version failed because it had light coming from the top-left AND bottom-right simultaneously on every one of a hundred elements. Colour is rationed to the point of austerity: exactly one hue family exists on the page (terracotta #d97757 for fills and LEDs, #e08a68 as its text tint, #e0a355 as its amber sibling), and even the mock macOS traffic lights and dock icons get pulled back with a saturate filter so nothing competes — when the brand orange appears, it is the only saturated thing in the viewport and it lands hard. The nostalgia comes from texture rather than costume: 1.6%-alpha scanlines, a 5.5% SVG grain, an amber phosphor clock in the tray with a real glow, a lit LED in every title bar. And it earns the dark: body ink #efe6da is 14.9:1 on the window face, secondary #b9ac9c is 8.3:1, the faintest tier #8d8073 is 4.8:1, so it clears AA everywhere while still feeling low-lit rather than high-contrast.
